title: From Gravitational Action to Physical Scattering
overview: How far can an original gravitational action carry us from source-owned interactions and boundary data toward genuinely physical incoming and outgoing scattering states?
question: What additional boundary, constraint and asymptotic structures turn a source-derived kinematic scattering calculation into a physical scattering system?
foundation: Published Paper IX establishes the local nonlinear metric-response geometry derived from the same boundary-completed regulated gravitational action: the finite radiative packet observation has 21 new quadratic and 56 new cubic quotient directions, while a specified common Schwartz-profile observation achieves complete observed nonlinear response closure at second order. In parallel, the developing internal P9-SA11 scattering investigation constructs source-linked W6 one-particle and CH24 Bose-pair kinematic evolution, source-derived incoming/outgoing wave operators and a unitary kinematic comparison, with nonidentity proved for a small-coupling family.
limits: Paper IX proves source-specific nonlinear gravitational reconstruction and boundary geometry in a prescribed finite regulator; it does not establish a physical S-matrix. The separately developing P9-SA11 kinematic nonidentity result concerns sufficiently small positive real couplings, with the original unit-coupling claim open. The nonlinear future-frame W6 readback obstruction and the original released-boundary variation require an enlarged action-derived physical carrier, appropriate Euler/Cartan flux, and coupled Bose-pair/gauge/BRST preservation before physical or celestial scattering amplitudes can be inferred.
next: Develop a source-derived phase space with physically justified boundary equations and Cartan flux, incorporating any necessary extra geometric degrees of freedom; prove invariant W6/CH24 Bose-pair and gauge/BRST constraints; distinguish the original unit-coupling kinematic question from physical scattering, then test on-shell channels and celestial transform eligibility.
